description: Device CLI catalog. Legacy tab tools use the browser-ops adapter. computer_* tools use the separate approval-gated computer-control MCP bridge, never the legacy tab dispatcher. One JSON object per CLI call; ok must be true to confirm success.

tools.name: tabs_register
tools.description: Open and register a tab, or claim an existing tab, for the calling lane. A tab owned by another lane cannot be claimed.
tools.output: JSON: ok, target_id, url, title, owner.

tools.name: tabs_heartbeat
tools.description: Refresh the heartbeat on the calling lane's registered tabs, optionally just one target.

tools.name: tabs_mark_done
tools.description: Mark the calling lane's tabs done. Done tabs become eligible for sweeping.

tools.name: tabs_list
tools.description: List registered tabs with live titles, URLs, owners and lifecycle, plus unregistered page tabs.

tools.name: tabs_close_mine
tools.description: Close only the calling lane's registered tabs. Never close another lane's or unregistered tabs; preserve the last-tab guard.

tools.name: tabs_sweep_now
tools.description: Close done or stale registered tabs, prune missing targets and log actions. Never close unregistered or fresh-heartbeat tabs; preserve the last-tab guard.
tools.output: JSON: ok, closed, pruned, kept, remaining_page_tabs.

tools.name: screen_capture_tab
tools.description: Capture a PNG of an explicit browser tab, including a background tab.
tools.output: JSON: ok, target_id, path, bytes, title, url; host wrapper may add local_path.

tools.name: screen_capture_desktop
tools.description: Capture the Windows desktop through its configured interactive scheduled task.
tools.output: JSON: ok, path, bytes; host wrapper may add local_path.

tools.name: computer_look
tools.description: Read one explicit page's bounded visible element map, text, title, URL and viewport. No screenshot file or DOM writes.
tools.output: JSON: ok, target_id, elements, text, title, url, viewport.

tools.name: computer_screenshot
tools.description: Approval-gated tab screenshot, or full Windows desktop capture without a target.

tools.name: computer_click
tools.description: Click exactly one visible element. Text is an exact label; indices must come from a fresh look. Ambiguous matches fail.
tools.output: JSON: ok, target_id, action, dispatched. Dispatch is not proof of the intended page outcome.

tools.name: computer_type
tools.description: Type into a non-password input or textarea and read it back. No fallback to an unrelated field.
tools.output: JSON: ok, value_now, read_back_verified; failed read-back means inspect before retrying.

tools.name: computer_press
tools.description: Dispatch a supported key to the explicit tab. Modifiers are comma-separated ctrl, shift, alt or meta.

tools.name: computer_scroll
tools.description: Dispatch a wheel event at the tab viewport center. At least one nonzero delta; bounded to 4000 CSS pixels per axis.
tools.output: JSON: ok, target_id, action, dispatched. This does not verify that a container moved.

tools.name: computer_hover
tools.description: Move the browser pointer to exactly one visible element. Hover can trigger page actions, so approval is required.

tools.name: computer_drag
tools.description: Drag a pointer between distinct in-viewport CSS-pixel coordinates, using 2 to 60 steps. Native and HTML5 drag acceptance remains a separate device check.

tools.name: computer_open_app
tools.description: Request a configured allowed_apps alias on macOS or Windows. No arbitrary shell command, arguments or user-provided executable path.
tools.output: JSON: ok, application, launch_requested, verified_visible=false. A successful request is not proof the app is visible.
